===Recruiting=== Smith was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2022 class, according to major recruiting services. On September 29, 2021, he committed to head coach [[Eric Musselman]] and the [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas Razorbacks]], over other finalists [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]], [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]] and [[Arkansas–Pine Bluff Golden Lions men's basketball|Arkansas–Pine Bluff]]. Smith was projected to be a starting guard for the [[2022–23 Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball team|Arkansas Razorbacks]] for the 2022–23 season, though a persistent knee injury kept him sidelined for the majority of the season. Smith appeared in seventeen games, averaging 12.5 points per contest.{{cite web|title=Arkansas - Season Statistics|url=https://arkansasrazorbacks.com/stats/mbb/2022-23/teamcume.htm|website=arkansasrazorbacks.com|access-date=February 12, 2023}} He returned late in the season, helping Arkansas advance to the Sweet 16 in the [[2023 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]]. Arkansas defeated Illinois in the first round 73-63, and upset #1 seed Kansas in the second round, 72–71. Smith and the Hogs lost to eventual national champion Connecticut in the Sweet 16, 88–65. Arkansas finished the season 22–14. ==Professional career== ===Charlotte Hornets (2023–2025)=== Smith was selected with the 27th pick of the [[2023 NBA draft]] by the [[Charlotte Hornets]]{{cite web|title=Charlotte Hornets Add Four Players In 2023 NBA Draft|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/charlotte-hornets-add-four-players-in-2023-nba-draft|website=NBA.com|date=June 23, 2023|access-date=December 23, 2024}} and on July 2, he signed with the team.{{cite web|first=Miguel|last=Ramirez|title=Charlotte Hornets Sign Nick Smith Jr.|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/charlotte-hornets-sign-nick-smith-jr|website=NBA.com|date=July 2, 2023|access-date=December 23, 2024}} Smith made franchise history with the Hornets during his rookie season by finishing the year with a scorching 43.2% three-point shooting percentage, which placed him among the most efficient rookie shooters in franchise history. He became only the second NBA rookie ever—at age 19 or younger—to hit this efficiency threshold, joining Jayson Tatum (who shot 43.4% in 2017-18). Among all rookies in NBA History, his campaign remains near the top for high-volume, first-year marksmen. This exceptional mark led all rookies in 3-point percentage for the 2023-2024 season. Throughout his rookie and sophomore seasons, he was [[NBA G League#Standard assignment|assigned]] several times to the [[Greensboro Swarm]].{{cite web|title=2023-2024 Greensboro Swarm Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Greensboro-Swarm/45/Transaction_History/2024|website=RealGM.com|access-date=December 23, 2024}}{{cite web|title=2024-2025 Greensboro Swarm Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Greensboro-Swarm/45/Transaction_History/2025|website=RealGM.com|access-date=December 23, 2024}} Smith made 60 appearances (27 starts) for the Hornets during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 9.9 points, 2.1 rebounds, and 2.4 assists. Smith was waived by the Hornets on September 25, 2025.{{cite web|title= Charlotte Hornets Waive Nick Smith Jr. |url= https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/charlotte-hornets-waive-nick-smith-jr |website=NBA.com|date=September 25, 2025|access-date=September 25, 2025}} ===Los Angeles Lakers (2025–2026)=== On September 29, 2025, Smith signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{Cite web |last=Heyen |first=Billy |date=2025-09-29 |title=Lakers sign 21-year old former 1st-round pick who was inexplicably still a free agent |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/article/lakers-sign-21-old-former-165806995.html |access-date=2025-11-04 |website=Yahoo Sports |language=en-US}} Smith made franchise history by becoming the youngest player in Lakers history to score 25 or more points without attempting a single free throw. He achieved this during a standout performance against the Portland Trail Blazers. He also became the 6th player in Lakers franchise to record 25+ points, 5+ assists, and 5+ 3PM off the bench in a regular season game.
